Let me analyze this specification. It's about Spring Cloud Data Flow (s-c-d) — the user stories reference early Spring Cloud Data Flow history:

- U1: Upload custom modules using shell/rest-api — module registration/upload feature
- U2: Module registry flexibility — modules immediately reflected in module registry (dynamic registration instead of hard-coded bootstrap)
- U3-U8: Migrating modules from Spring XD to spring-cloud-stream-modules (s-c-s-m) / spring-cloud-stream (s-c-s) repos: jms, mail, mongo, mqtt, reactor-ip, stdout

So the software increment covers:
1. A module upload/registration feature in Spring Cloud Data Flow via shell and REST API
2. Refactoring the module registry to be dynamic/flexible (not hard-coded at bootstrap)
3. Migrating 6 modules from Spring XD to the new repos

Let me build a WBS:

**A. Requirements analysis & design**
- A1: Analyze requirements, review existing ModuleRegistryPopulator, XD modules
- A2: Design dynamic module registry and upload API (REST + shell)

**B. Dynamic module registry (U2)**
- B1: Implement registry SPI/service allowing runtime registration
- B2: Refactor bootstrap populator to use the registry service
- B3: Unit tests for registry

**C. Upload via REST API (U1, part)**
- C1: Implement REST endpoint for module upload/registration (controller)
- C2: Integration tests for REST endpoint

**D. Shell commands (U1, part)**
- D1: Implement shell commands for module upload/registration
- D2: Shell tests

**E. Module migrations (U3-U8)** — 6 modules:
- jms (source) — move to s-c-s-m
- mail (source) — s-c-s-m
- mongo (source) — s-c-s-m
- mqtt (source) — s-c-s
- reactor-ip (source, likely TCP/UDP based on reactor) — s-c-s
- stdout (sink? Actually "stdout" in XD was a sink, but story says "use it as source"... spec says "so I can use it as source to build streaming pipeline" for all. But I'll just treat each as a module migration.)

Each module migration: port code from XD, adapt to Spring Cloud Stream programming model (Binder abstraction, @EnableBinding), create Maven project structure, configuration properties, tests.

Some modules are more complex (jms, reactor-ip) than others (stdout, mail).

**F. Documentation & build/release**
- F1: Update docs (reference docs, README)
- F2: Build/CI configuration for new repos/modules
- F3: Final integration verification, QA, bug fixing

Let me assign effort estimates (work-hours). Assume a single developer, experienced with Spring, Java 17, Spring Cloud Stream/Data Flow.

Estimates:

1. Requirements analysis & design: 16 h
2. Design of dynamic registry + upload API: included above or separate 12 h

- ACT-01: Requirements analysis and design of dynamic module registry & upload mechanism: 24 h

- ACT-09: Migrate mail module: 16 h

- ACT-11: Migrate mqtt module: 20 h
- ACT-12: Migrate reactor-ip module: 24 h (reactor-based TCP/UDP, more complex)
- ACT-13: Migrate stdout module: 8 h (simple)
- ACT-14: Build/CI setup, Maven project scaffolding for new modules: 8 h — maybe fold into each module. Keep separate small.
- ACT-15: Documentation updates (reference docs, README, shell help): 12 h
- ACT-16: End-to-end integration testing & bug fixing: 24 h

- "Upload custom modules" = registering module coordinates (Maven coordinates / URI) via REST/shell rather than binary file upload with artifact hosting; artifacts resolvable from Maven repository. I'll assume registration of Maven coordinates/URIs, plus optionally resolving; file upload to server not required. Record assumption.
- Registry persistence: in-memory (as original Data Flow initial implementation); modules immediately visible after registration.
- Module migrations include adapting to Spring Cloud Stream annotation model (@EnableBinding, Source/Sink channels), Spring Boot auto-configuration, properties classes, unit + integration tests with embedded brokers (ActiveMQ/embedded Mongo via Fongo or real, Mosquitto for MQTT, etc.), and Maven project setup in target repos.
- Target repos: s-c-s-m = spring-cloud-stream-modules (actually renamed spring-cloud-stream-app-starters later); s-c-s = spring-cloud-stream.

- Estimate excludes deployment to production and release management beyond CI config.
- MQTT/reactor-ip tests use lightweight embedded servers/mocks.

Technical decisions:
- REST endpoint POST /modules (or /apps) with coordinates; shell command wraps REST client.
- Registry as a service interface (ModuleRegistry) with in-memory implementation; bootstrap populator delegates to it so registrations appear immediately.
- Maven coordinates (group:artifact:version) as module identifiers; resolution via Spring's Maven infrastructure (Aether) — historically spring-cloud-dataflow used maven resolver.
- Modules migrated to Spring Cloud Stream model with @EnableBinding(Source.class), Spring Boot auto-config, @ConfigurationProperties for options, whitelisted properties.
- Testing: JUnit 5, Mockito, Testcontainers/embedded brokers for integration tests.

technical_and_design_decisions: Implement a dynamic ModuleRegistry service interface (with an in-memory default implementation) that supports runtime registration/unregistration of modules; refactor the existing hard-coded ModuleRegistryPopulator to delegate to this service so newly contributed modules are immediately visible in the registry (U2).

Expose module upload/registration through a REST API (POST/DELETE on a module resource, e.g., /modules) that accepts module coordinates (Maven group:artifact:version) and/or a resolvable URI; artifacts are resolved through the project's existing Maven resolution infrastructure rather than hosting binary uploads on the server (U1).
Implement shell commands (e.g., 'module register'/'module upload') as thin clients that invoke the new REST API, reusing the existing shell-to-REST communication layer (U1).

Migrate each Spring XD module to the Spring Cloud Stream programming model: @EnableBinding with Source/Sink channels, Spring Boot auto-configuration classes, and @ConfigurationProperties option classes with whitelisted properties (U3-U8).

Structure each migrated module as a standalone Maven project in the target repository (spring-cloud-stream-modules for jms, mail, mongo; spring-cloud-stream for mqtt, reactor-ip, stdout) with its own build descriptor.

Use JUnit 5 + Mockito for unit tests and embedded/lightweight brokers or servers for integration tests (embedded ActiveMQ for JMS, GreenMail or stub SMTP for mail, embedded MongoDB for mongo, embedded Mosquitto/broker stub for MQTT, local TCP/UDP sockets for reactor-ip).
Baseline technology stack: Java 17, Spring Framework 6 / Spring Boot 3, consistent with the specification's stated minimum requirements.
All development tasks (implementation, testing, documentation, build/CI configuration) are performed by a single developer, consistent with the assignment.
assumptions: 'Upload custom modules' means registering a module's Maven coordinates or URI with the data flow server via shell/REST so it becomes usable in stream/task definitions; no server-side binary artifact repository or file-storage subsystem is required.
The module registry keeps registrations in memory (matching the behavior of the initial implementation); persistence of registrations across server restarts is out of scope for this increment.

Each XD module migration includes: porting the production code, adapting it to the Spring Cloud Stream binder model, creating option/properties classes, unit tests, integration tests, and Maven project scaffolding in the target repository.
The six modules to migrate (jms, mail, mongo, mqtt, reactor-ip, stdout) exist in the Spring XD codebase and are functionally stable, so no new feature design is needed, only porting and adaptation.
s-c-s-m refers to the spring-cloud-stream-modules repository and s-c-s to the spring-cloud-stream repository.
The developer is experienced with Spring, Spring XD, and Spring Cloud Stream/Data Flow internals, so no significant learning-curve allowance is included.
Estimates cover development effort only (design, coding, testing, documentation, CI setup); they exclude release management, production deployment, and post-release support.
Code review, where applicable, is lightweight self-review performed within the implementation activities.
Reasonable test coverage (unit plus integration) is required for all deliverables; no separate QA team is involved.

activities.activity_description: Analyze user stories U1-U8, review the existing ModuleRegistryPopulator and XD module code, and produce the design for the dynamic module registry, the module upload REST/shell interfaces, and the module migration approach (Spring Cloud Stream model, configuration properties, testing strategy).

Implement the ModuleRegistry service supporting runtime registration/unregistration with immediate visibility, and refactor the hard-coded bootstrap populator to delegate to it so contributed modules instantly appear in the registry.
Write unit tests covering registration, unregistration, duplicate handling, lookup, and immediate reflection of changes in stream/task definition resolution.

activities.activity_name: U1 - REST API for module upload/registration
activities.activity_description: Implement the REST controller, request/response DTOs, validation, error handling, and wiring to the dynamic registry and Maven artifact resolution for uploading/registering custom modules.
Write integration tests for the upload/registration endpoints, including success, validation failure, and unresolvable-coordinate scenarios.

activities.activity_name: U1 - Shell commands for module upload/registration
activities.activity_description: Implement shell commands (e.g., module register/upload/list/unregister) that invoke the new REST API, including command options, help text, and result formatting.
Write tests for the new shell commands covering argument parsing, REST interaction, and output rendering.

activities.activity_name: U3 - Migrate jms module to spring-cloud-stream-modules
activities.activity_description: Port the JMS module from Spring XD to the Spring Cloud Stream source model: code migration, auto-configuration, properties classes, Maven project setup, and unit/integration tests with an embedded broker.

activities.activity_name: U4 - Migrate mail module to spring-cloud-stream-modules
activities.activity_description: Port the mail module from Spring XD to the Spring Cloud Stream source model, including auto-configuration, properties, project setup, and tests with a stub/embedded mail server.

activities.activity_name: U5 - Migrate mongo module to spring-cloud-stream-modules
activities.activity_description: Port the mongo module from Spring XD to the Spring Cloud Stream source model, including auto-configuration, properties, project setup, and tests against embedded MongoDB.

activities.activity_name: U6 - Migrate mqtt module to spring-cloud-stream
activities.activity_description: Port the mqtt module from Spring XD to the Spring Cloud Stream source model, including auto-configuration, properties, project setup, and tests with an embedded/stub MQTT broker.

activities.activity_name: U7 - Migrate reactor-ip module to spring-cloud-stream
activities.activity_description: Port the reactor-based TCP/UDP IP module from Spring XD to the Spring Cloud Stream source model, adapting reactive connection handling, auto-configuration, properties, project setup, and socket-level integration tests.

activities.activity_name: U8 - Migrate stdout module to spring-cloud-stream
activities.activity_description: Port the simple stdout module from Spring XD to the Spring Cloud Stream model, including minimal auto-configuration, project setup, and tests.

activities.activity_name: Build and CI configuration for new modules and endpoints
activities.activity_description: Configure parent POMs, module build descriptors, dependency management, and continuous-integration build definitions for the migrated modules and the updated data flow components.
Update reference documentation and READMEs: dynamic registry behavior, module upload via REST/shell usage examples, and per-module configuration property documentation.

activities.activity_name: End-to-end integration verification and defect fixing
activities.activity_description: Perform end-to-end verification: register an uploaded custom module via shell and REST, confirm immediate registry visibility, and build streaming pipelines using each migrated module; fix defects found.
